fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Detached Structure
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with posts or reflective delineators on both sides to make it visible at night or in low-visibility conditions.
• Trim trees and shrubs along both sides of the driveway so emergency vehicles can travel its full length without obstruction.
• Maintain a minimum vertical clearance along the driveway to allow ladder trucks and other tall emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Create a turnaround area near the main residence so fire engines and other large vehicles can reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Keep the turnaround area clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and stored materials at all times.
• Trim dense vegetation near the detached structure so responders can reach and move around all sides of it.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings on foot.
• Post the property address visibly at both the road and near the main residence so responders can confirm they have reached the correct location.
• Identify and communicate the single access point limitation to your local fire department so they can note it in pre-incident planning records.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Open Terrain; Brush Area; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Single Access Route; Limited Vegetation Separation; Grass Cover; Brush Concentration
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim all shrubs that are directly touching or within a few feet of the house walls.
• Remove brush concentrated near the base of the structure on all sides.
• Thin scattered trees close to the house so their branches do not hang over the roof or walls.
• Clear grass and low ground cover within the immediate area surrounding the structure.
• Separate shrubs from each other near the house so fire cannot move easily from one plant to the next.
• Remove dead or dry grass and brush from around any outbuildings or secondary structures on the property.
• Cut back vegetation along the single access route so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep the driveway clear of overhanging branches that could block emergency vehicle access.
• Thin brush concentrations visible in open terrain areas closest to the structure.
• Remove grass and low brush from the edges of the driveway to reduce fire contact with the access route.
• Clear a visible open area between the surrounding vegetation and the structure on all sides.
• Keep scattered shrubs in open terrain areas near the house cut low to reduce the amount of material that can burn close to the structure.
